statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is 7% in the low band roughly four and a half hours into the Sunday Globex session, after NQ retraced off its session high.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow evidence-based danger window is flagged over 13:00-15:00 UTC, the window containing Monday's US cash open, where an opening-auction imbalance can extend before it retraces. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ backs about 51 points off the 30,130.50 session high to 30,079.50 (+0.54%), ending the three-hour extension; Tail eases to 7% and Stress to 33% as US-China preparatory talks are reported successful
body:
About four and a half hours into the Globex session the price path has changed character. NQ prints 30,079.50, up 162.25 points (+0.54%) against the 29,917.25 Friday settle, inside an observed 29,904.50-30,130.50 range, and the Investing.com feed corroborates 30,076.25 at the same 02:16 UTC stamp. The index is now roughly 51 points below its session high rather than 18, and the run of three consecutive higher hours has ended. That is an observed retracement away from a session extreme, which is the mean reversion this Tail measure is defined against, so the one amplifier carried in the previous hour has resolved and Tail eases to 7%.

The cash reference is still Friday's NDX close at 29,644.17, up 0.67%, set inside a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range in a tape where the S&P 500 added 0.17% and the Dow shed 0.18%. Internals were split rather than aligned. The shared Finviz context for this run is again only partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, and at 112 minutes old it is outside the freshness bound, so it is treated as stale context and not relied upon; the independent research below stands on its own. What the latest-session part of it argued - megacaps evenly divided four to four, Technology up 0.84% against Communication Services down 0.74%, semiconductors positive five to two - is dispersion and rotation rather than index-level one-way structure, and nothing in the live evidence contradicts that.

The energy complex has stabilised without reversing. WTI trades at $98.26, down 2.03%, and Brent at $101.87, down 1.92%, still a fourth consecutive session of declines attributed to diplomatic efforts that could restore regional energy flows, with US-Iran contacts discussed around the UN General Assembly. Crude has ticked up about thirty cents from the previous hour against verified weekend escalation - Houthi missile and drone strikes on Riyadh, a Trump warning to Iran of dire economic and political consequences absent a deal, and Tehran threatening sustained retaliation - but a complex that closes a session two percent lower into that news is pricing the diplomatic branch. The escalation is therefore carried as Stress and headline-gap risk, not as an established Tail path.

The rate backdrop is unchanged and remains the heaviest standing weight. The FOMC raised rates 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, its first hike in three years, and signalled at least one more this year. The 10-year sits at 5.00% as of the 18 September close, up six basis points and a level last seen in 2007, having topped 5.04% earlier in the week, against 4.75% at the 2-year; the latest H.15 observation, dated 17 September, reads 4.67% and 4.94%. Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is too high in all aspects of the economy, beyond just oil prices and widely in services, and supported the unanimous vote to hike. VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08%, a calm reading against that backdrop.

The week's principal catalyst resolved one stage further overnight. Bessent and Greer met Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York on Sunday on artificial intelligence, tariffs and critical minerals, and Bessent afterwards described the meeting as successful, with the US proposing a US-China AI Dialogue and a notification mechanism for AI incidents rising to national-security level. The Trump-Xi summit is confirmed for 24 September in Washington. A preparatory round that concludes constructively narrows the dispersion carried into the summit rather than widening it, which is the marginal reason Stress eases a point. Monday's own calendar is light: a Goolsbee speech at 10:30 UTC, the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30 UTC and bill auctions at 15:30 UTC.

Net: Tail 7%, down two points, because the session-high hold that was the sole amplifier has been replaced by an observed pullback and the excursion still spans only 0.76% on a thin Sunday book. The mapped state stays EA_ON and green. Stress eases to 33% on the constructive preparatory-talks readout, against an unchanged 5.00% 10-year and a Fed that has just resumed hiking. Confidence rises to 78% on two live futures feeds agreeing within 3.25 points, verified oil, yield and volatility levels, a seven-day US calendar re-verified in this run and extended through 28 September, and multiple independently verified weekend reports; it is discounted for the absence of live cash-market cross-asset confirmation over the weekend and for Finviz context that is both partial and stale.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available and describe an unbroken low-Tail regime across the Sunday of the weekend halt and into the Globex reopen. Tail held between 4% and 9% in every hour, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout, and rose only in the closing hours as the reopen produced its first live price path, peaking at 9% in the most recent slot. Stress drifted from 25% early on 20 September into a 30-35% band as the post-hike rate backdrop and the elevated oil complex accumulated, easing to 34% in the final hour. Confidence ranged from 70% to 77%, dipping in the deepest part of the halt when no live price path existed and recovering once futures reopened. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours. The present assessment breaks the upward Tail drift at 7% as the extension unwinds.
outlookSummary: The cycle covers the remainder of the Asian session, the European session, the Monday US cash session through the 20:00 UTC close, the CME maintenance halt and the Tuesday Globex reopen. Tail is projected to stay inside the low band in all 24 hours, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON throughout. The projected peak is 12% in the hour containing the 13:30 UTC US cash open, followed by 11% in the hour after it, which is why the flagged danger window spans 13:00-15:00 UTC; secondary 10% readings fall on the 12:30 UTC Chicago Fed release, the 15:30 UTC bill auctions and the closing hour into 20:00 UTC. The cycle low of 6% falls in the 21:00-22:00 UTC maintenance halt, when no NQ price path exists and a no-retracement trend is mechanically impossible. Stress is projected between 33% and 37%, held up by a 5.00% 10-year and a Fed that has just resumed hiking, and capped by a fourth consecutive decline in crude and a constructive US-China preparatory round. Confidence decays from 78% to 68% across the cycle as the evidence base ages. These are conditional projections: no future price-path structure is treated as already observed, and an upgrade would require observed shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements.
